items.paper: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness
items.figure: Figure 1, memory hierarchy and tiling panels
features: Matrices are data glyphs with aspect and block divisions; Q, K-transpose, V, and output retain distinct positions.
One current tile is highlighted while the full attention matrix is a dotted conceptual region, not a hardware container.
Outer and inner traversal use distinct arrows; HBM copies are distinct from on-chip tile computation.
The crop excludes the runtime chart so composition cues cannot accidentally invent performance claims.
Encoder and decoder are two stable vertical columns with a shared bottom-to-top reading direction.
Residual rails stay outside the corresponding operation and join at the explicit Add and Norm block.
Repeated stacks use one representative enclosure and an N-times label rather than drawing every layer.
The encoder-to-decoder cross-attention input is routed as one distinct bridge, not a generic global bus.
Q and K enter the first MatMul through separate short input lines; V bypasses the score path and enters the final MatMul.
MatMul, scaling, optional mask, SoftMax, and final MatMul form a compact operator chain with semantic color roles.
Several projected attention heads are represented by offset repeats, one h label, and a single Concat merge.
The primitive operator view and repeated-head view are aligned side by side, each answering a different level of explanation.

items.paper: Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces
features: Previous and next hidden state sit at opposite ends of one long horizontal state rail, with channels kept parallel.
Current input and output use compact vector glyphs below the state rail instead of undifferentiated boxes.
Selection-derived parameter feeders form a separate lower rail and enter their corresponding state operators.
State expansion, input transformation, and readout remain spatially distinct; the overview does not unroll every timestep.

items.paper: Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces
features: H3, Gated MLP, and Mamba reuse the same frame, input origin, output position, and operator vocabulary for comparison.
Linear projection, sequence transformation, and nonlinear operators use different shape roles rather than only different colors.
The content path and gate path split at the bottom and merge at one explicit multiplication circle.
Small activation circles and short gate feeders avoid implying that a gate is a full hardware module.

items.paper: Transformers are SSMs: Generalized Models and Efficient Algorithms Through Structured State Space Duality
features: Sequential and parallel projection designs use identical frames, operator colors, and output alignment.
Parameter projections relocate to the input stage in the parallel block, making the dependency difference visible without prose.
The gate bypass is a quiet side rail, while SSM and convolution remain on the principal branch.
Normalization, multiplication, and activation are small distinct operator circles with a concise common legend.

items.paper: U-Net: Convolutional Networks for Biomedical Image Segmentation
features: The contracting and expanding paths are mirrored in a U shape; spatial resolution determines vertical level.
Feature maps use changing aspect and thickness with channel counts and spatial sizes, not identical process rectangles.
Skip-feature copies bridge only matching resolutions, leaving a clear central corridor between the two paths.
Filled and outlined feature maps distinguish resident and copied features; a compact arrow legend identifies operations.

items.paper: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
features: A two-operation principal branch and one identity bypass explain the mechanism with almost no enclosure.
The bypass rejoins at a visible plus-circle; the output activation is placed after the merge, not before it.
The short x, F(x), and F(x)+x labels name values separately from the weight-layer operations.
Monochrome strokes and generous whitespace make data dependency carry the explanation without decorative effects.

items.paper: FlashAttention-3: Fast and Accurate Attention with Asynchrony and Low-precision
features: Two warpgroups have separate resource rows on one left-to-right time axis.
Matching iteration colors track the same work across GEMM0, Softmax, and GEMM1 rather than assigning a new color to every operation.
Vertical dashed separators align overlap boundaries; each row retains its own ordered operation sequence.
This is a supplied schedule explanation: bar widths and overlap must not be invented for an unspecified algorithm.

items.paper: Learning Fast Algorithms for Linear Transforms Using Butterfly Factorizations
features: Four equal-size sparse-matrix views expose how nonzero structure changes between factors.
One red mark color and a common matrix coordinate frame make the recursive block patterns comparable.
The progression from coarse to fine block structure is the visual subject; no decorative process modules are added.
These are factor sparsity views, not an FFT signal-flow graph; actual permutation and twiddle dependencies need source data.
